remit: X12 defines this reason as expenses incurred after coverage terminated.
metaDescription: CO-27 denial explained: expenses incurred after coverage terminated. How to check eligibility on the date of service, rebill the right payer and prevent it.
summary: The payer says the patient's coverage had ended before the date of service.
causes: Eligibility was not checked for the date of service
The patient changed or lost insurance and did not tell the office
A plan year or enrollment period changed
fixes: Run an eligibility check for the exact date of service
If the patient had other coverage, bill that payer
If there was no coverage, follow your financial policy for patient balances
prevention: Verify eligibility before each visit, not just at the first one
Ask patients to report any plan change before they arrive

faqs.question: How early should eligibility be checked?
faqs.answer: Before the visit and again on the date of service where the schedule allows. Coverage can change between booking and arrival.

faqs.question: Can CO-27 be appealed?
faqs.answer: Only if the payer's records are wrong. Proof of active coverage on the date of service is what an appeal needs.
